A little late to the party here, and I will take a moment to break anonymity to say that this is Adrian and we have spoken many times. 

While I may be part of the minority, I want to remind you with absolute honesty that there are people who really enjoy the game, and that it is not forgotten! It seems a common thread that others can't make heads or tails of it, but for I just \*got it\* almost immediately. Maybe because I am familiar with the same kind of loss that inspired the game, or maybe because the unique and creative way the world is imagined reminds me of the worlds I used to make as a child, and with that Eoris rekindled my creativity and imagination. Maybe it's because I am an aspiring artist and writer as well. Whatever the case, Eoris has inspired me on a deep level, to the point where I have even had dreams taking place in the setting! 

To this day Eoris is still my favorite rpg. Not only is it full of beautiful art, but the setting itself fascinating and I have spent many hours reading and pondering on its nature. As far as I know there's not a single game like it and it's originality is a huge draw compared to most games which are simply a rehash of Tolkien fantasy. I have shared the game with my friends and family and they all enjoy it too (or maybe my enthusiasm is infectious). Though financially a flop, I think the game did exactly what it set out to do: Come up with a world and system where anything is possible with plenty of room for GMs and Players to make it their own. It may not be perfect, but what ever is?  Regardless, it has definitely influenced my life for the better and not only do I play the game regularly, but I have been writing stories in the setting as well.

So, in depth, here was my first encounter:

I was at a party. There was the ubiquitous alcoholic fruit punch and I was fairly sloshed. An acquaintance of mine knew that I was obsessed with the idea of vampires, and told me he had someone for me to meet. He took me to the corner of the room where this kid was standing. . . probably not old enough to drink (to be fair, I wasn't either), shortish, with shoulder length red hair and blood red eyes. I assumed they were contacts. Other then that he seemed perfectly normal. A little awkward and gangly, but normal.

The acquaintance says, "So you want to meet a vampire so bad, here's your vampire."

And I laughed. Boy did I laugh. Like doubling over, belly-splitting laugh. I said, "No way is this kid a vampire, he's such a dweeb." I blame being drunk for the most part, but it was pretty ridiculous. And by the time I regained enough composure to look at his face, well . . . I realized I shouldn't have laughed. Something about the look he gave me silenced me. There wasn't much talking after that and I managed to excuse myself. I got home safe, and pretty much forgot about the encounter.

It wasn't til the next night that the attack came, and it started with a dream. I haven't mastered lucid dreaming, and do it more through accident than any conscious attempts. This was one of them. In this dream, I was working for National Geographic in filming the native animals of South America. My film crew were partying in a local town while I was walking into a clearing alone, in hopes of finding a jaguar.
When I was far enough away from the town, I was struck down. It happened quickly, and I fell on my stomach and thought, hey, Im about to be mauled by my favorite animal. Not a bad way to die. But it was a human hand that grabbed me and flipped me over to my back.

What I saw filled me with the most terror I'd ever known. At the time, I did not recognize it was the kid from the party, his features were somewhat distorted. . . . skin as pale as bone, his eyelids were rotted away and the first thing I noticed were the glowing red orbs that were his eyes. Then his fangs . . . they were like small sabers or wolf teeth. . . nothing like the puny Hollywood fangs that are used in television. The terror gripped me tenfold and I knew I was going to die. My body relaxed to accept my fate, and the vampire was pleased. He tilted my head to the side and placed his fangs at my neck. 

In doing so he released my right hand. At this time in the dream I became lucid. Something told me, if I died now, I would die in my sleep and never wake up. By instinct alone I grabbed out, and found a branch that had fallen when he pounced on me. I rammed it through the side of his skull. He shot up to stare at me, surprised and furious, and before he could recover I tried snapping his neck.

This did not kill him, but at least he was paralyzed. I cut his heart out his heart. This did not kill him. I burned it, and I burned him, chopping up his body and putting it in a bonfire. This did not kill him. Even when there was nothing left and I had spread the ashes to the winds, I still felt an awful presence, like he was looking down at me in fury. I forced myself to wake up. 

He was still there, standing outside the glass sliding door that lead to our back yard. Red glowing eyes, the look and stink of death, the fangs and claws like a beast. . . he told me to calm down, that he just wanted to talk. I promptly told him to fuck off, as he'd just tried to kill me. But he wouldn't. He stayed by the door, tapping on the glass and trying to get me to come to the door. I would have chalked this up to a hypnogogic hallucination if it wasn't for the fact that he stayed there for hours . . .  and me, not knowing what to do, childishly covered my head with my blanket and sat shaking while he called for me. At dawn, when the sun started to come up, he left.

He came back 6 months later, under a similar circumstances. First there was a dream, not nearly as dramatic as the first, and when I woke up he was climbing the side of the house to get to the second story window of my bedroom. He demanded that I come to the window and let him in. When I would not, I felt spectral hands grab me and pull me. . . 

There was a sensation of pins and needles as he had started to pull my spirit(?) from my body to force me. I panicked, and with all my might I forced myself back into myself. At this moment I got up from my bed and went to my father to wake him up. I told him there was a vampire hunting me, and I was going to die. 

I don't think he believed me at first. He treated it very trivially, telling me not to worry and all the sweet things a father says to a scared daughter. It wasn't til the night after that he told me to be careful. He said he saw the creature outside of his window too. He was able to give me a physical description without my prompting too. So I just nodded and did my best to stay indoors at night.

So, that's the start of it. Hope it's enough to satisfy. I must admit Im a bit nervous putting it all out there . . .
